@@100402070 <p> Notwithstanding the vying complexities , uncertainties and volatilities inherent in a rapidly changing 21st Century , with striking advances in artificial intelligence towards noble and ignoble ends , vast trans-continental demographic shifts , serious political conflict , the advent of virulent unforeseen diseases and pandemics , today 's thesis emphasises the need for scientists and non-scientists to quickly sharpen their understanding of genomics.And , crucially , its readiness and capacity for identifying , treating and curing bugs . Strategically , genomics should meaningfully engage the attention of health care policy experts especially in those developing countries where , less attention has been paid so far . <p> Within the purview of molecular biology , genomics analyses the comprehensive or partial genetic or epigenetic categorisation of organisms , and efforts to properly grasp the configuration and purpose of these categorisations and related biological products including complex molecules , microorganisms , plant cells , animal cells etc . Human health is the focus here and genomics , in that realm , assesses molecular dynamics , the interoperability of these molecular insights , emanating health interventions , impacts thereof and environmental factors in diseases . <p> According to the Journal of @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ 3 ) : 442-448 ) , a genome is the totality of an organism 's genetic makeup . It is a comprehensive set of deoxyribonuclenic acid ( DNA ) with a living cell . Typically , human cells contain approximately three billion base pairs of DNA , which makes the genome . On the other hand , viruses have their genetic composition via the ribonucleic acid ( RNA ) . <p> By the function of simple logical analysis , the ribonucleic acid appertains to the human DNA and the RNA upon which viruses derive their genetic attributes . So , there is a relationship , and the nature , scale , type , complexity , sequencing of such , is what genomics seeks to tackle . <p> Therefore , human genomics is but one part of genomics that 's relevant to human health . The human genome interrelates with a variety of other organisms , including pathogens , plants , and vectors . Upon that premise , genomics is evaluated across all organisms , as relevant to public health in human populations . For clarity , genomics is not to @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , tackles all genes and their interoperability to evaluate their brigaded influence , if any , on the growth and sustenance of organisms ; whereas , genetics assesses heredity and the functionalities of the single gene . <p> So , what 's hyperconnectivity got to do with genomics ? Everything ! Hyperconnectivity is a term that 's often associated with technology relative to multiple means of communications including , but not limited to , 5G , wireless applications , the internet of things , emails , social media , interoperable telephony etc . However , that 's not the strict sense in which the term is deployed in this article . Here , hyperconnectivity implies the relative accessibility of the phenomenal potentialities of genomic biotechnologies and capabilities in an interconnected world notwithstanding the income disparities between richer and poorer countries . <p> In other words , the beneficial offerings of genomics should be accessible to everyone if the overarching objective is better healthcare for all . More simply , people interact within and outside national boundaries . According to the United Nations World Tourism Organisation , pre-pandemic , 1.5 billion @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ world 's estimated 7.7 billion people in that year . The COVID-19 pandemic is evidence of the significant risk of the transmission of viruses within and beyond local frontiers hence on the one hand , and the hyperconnectivity of people globally on the other . <p> Of course , this does not negate the vast intellectual input , financial , research and development investments made by wealthier countries in genomic development ; which , in turn , rightly demands a return on investment , given the orthodoxy of the prevalent capitalist global model . Even so , the ethical imperatives of relative global health equity justify the wider accessibility of genomic advancements . <p> Does this proposition imply a do-nothing-approach on the part of poorer countries ? No ! What should it imply ? A re-prioritisation of healthcare investments , research and development , more effective and scalable international collaboration on genomic biotechnologies ; as nasty bugs emerge ( as they are sure to ! ) , partly due to adverse human interactions with linked ecosystems , drug resistant viruses and mutations thereof . It ca n't be business as @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ achievements , not least by enabling scientists to better comprehend biomolecules , enzymes , genes and polypeptides , and how they regulate cell development and functionalities . <p> Take CRISPR gene editing for instance . This is a genetic engineering methodology in molecular biology enabling targeted genome modification of living organisms . CRISPR 's attraction within the realms of biotechnology and medicine lies in its relative precision , affordability , and ease of deployment especially concerning in vivo gene editing . It offers vast potentials in the creation of new medicines to combat diseases like cancer , advances in agricultural products , genetically modified organisms , and the control of pathogens and pests . For their sparkling endeavours , CRISPR 's developers , Professor Jennifer Doudna ( University of California , Berkeley ) and Professor Emmanuelle Charpentier ( Max Planck Institute , Berlin ) , received the Nobel Prize for Chemistry in 2020 . <p> Based on revolutionary genomics , botanists have developed innovative approaches to creating disease and heat resistant crops . According to the International Monetary Fund 's Climate Change and Chronic Food Insecurity Report 2022 , food @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ projects that a minimum of 123 million people ( 12% ) of the SSA 's demographics ) would experience some form of food insecurity and malnutrition over the short to medium term . Scalable genomics in this realm is not only welcome , but could play a significant role in addressing food insecurity , in concert with other important interventions on the socio-political front . <p> Be that as it may , the international scientific research initiative , the Human Genome Project ( HGP ) , in 2003 , surfaced 92% or three billion base pairs of DNA found in every set of human chromosomes . At the time , those findings , and the dissemination , were almost overrun by disputes over intellectual property rights . Ultimately , global pressure and realism prevailed , resulting the unveiling of the HGP 's findings , which has proven to be seminal in other major genomics ' research projects . @@100402492 <h> ANALYSIS : Usefulness of mangroves in fight against climate change <p> Climate change is the long-term shift in temperature and weather patterns caused by natural processes and human activities such as deforestation and the burning of fossil fuels . <p> One of the most significant drivers of climate change is carbon emissions -- the burning of fossil fuels like coal , oil , and gas releases carbon dioxide into the atmosphere . This traps heat from the sun , causing the earth 's temperature to rise ; this is known as the greenhouse effect . The more carbon dioxide is released , the more the earth 's temperature rises , leading to more severe climate change . <p> The impacts of climate change can be devastating and one of the most visible effects is the increase in extreme weather events like droughts , heatwaves , and floods . These events can have serious consequences for communities around the world , causing damage to homes and infrastructure , disrupting food supplies , and increasing the risk of disease outbreaks . <p> Mangroves are one of the natural resources that can help mitigate the impacts of climate change . They @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ their roots and soil . Mangroves are some of the most efficient carbon sinks on the planet , storing up to four times more carbon per hectare than tropical rainforests . They are also able to protect coastlines from erosion and storm surges , which can be intensified by climate change . According to the UN Environment Programme ( UNEP ) , emissions resulting from mangrove losses make up nearly one-fifth of global emissions from deforestation . <p> Advertisement <p> WHAT ARE MANGROVES ? <p> Mangroves on water surface <p> Mangroves are a group of trees and shrubs that grow in tropical and subtropical coastal areas . They have unique adaptations to survive in saltwater , such as specialised roots that can filter out salt and leaves that excrete salt . <p> Mangroves are found in over 100 countries and have a unique ecosystem that supports a variety of wildlife and marine life , including birds , fish , and crustaceans . They also provide a habitat for endangered species such as sea turtles , manatees , and crocodiles . Although mangroves make up less than one percent of all @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ providing an array of essential goods and services which contribute significantly to the livelihoods , well-being and security of coastal communities . <p> Advertisement <p> The global average carbon stock of mangroves is around 1,000 tonnes of carbon per hectare , including soil carbon . If released back into the atmosphere , the resulting emissions would be the equivalent of travelling 26 million kilometres by car -- 650 times worldwide . <p> The mangrove forests in Nigeria are some of the largest and most diverse in the world . They are mainly found in the Niger Delta region -- making up the largest in Africa and the third largest in the world , stretching along the coast and covering about nine states . <p> The forests are known for their high biodiversity and they have significant economic importance for local communities . They are a source of food , medicine , and building materials . For example , the bark of the mangrove tree is used to make rope , while the wood is used to build houses and boats . The mangroves also support important fisheries , such as @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and food for local communities . <p> IMPORTANCE OF MANGROVES IN MITIGATING CLIMATE CRISIS <p> Advertisement <p> Mangrove trees in Nembe community , Bayelsa , Niger Delta area of Nigeria , drying up due to oil spills <p> Preserving mangroves has many advantages such as mitigating the impact of climate change , offering critical ecosystem protection , and providing socio-economic benefits . <p> Coastal defence : Mangrove forests act as natural buffers against storm surges , tsunamis , and erosion , reducing the impacts of extreme weather events intensified by climate change . Mangroves offer low-cost risk reduction in the face of rising sea levels and changes in storm frequency and intensity . They help reduce the risk from tropical cyclones -- that cause loss of life and damage to properties and infrastructures -- by decreasing the action of waves and impacts of flooding . Research by UNEP has demonstrated that mangroves ' robust build efficiently reduces storms ' destructive capabilities and wind surges by 70 to 90 percent . <p> Carbon sequestration : Mangroves are highly efficient carbon sinks , capable of sequestering large amounts of carbon dioxide from @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . The bulk of mangrove carbon is held in the soil , ranging from about 83 to almost 99 percent of the carbon stored in mangroves . They are able to sequester carbon at a rate that is up to five times higher than other tropical forests , due to their unique adaptations to grow in saline environments . The roots of mangroves are able to trap and store large amounts of organic matter , which can help to build up soil carbon over time . If undisturbed , the carbon can remain stable for centuries or more . In addition , the dense canopy of mangroves can help to reduce the amount of sunlight that reaches the forest floor , which can slow the rate of decomposition and increase the amount of carbon stored in the soil . <p> Water filtration : Mangrove roots and soil help to protect the health of surrounding ecosystems by acting as a water filter while also improving water quality . This filtration is enabled by the mangrove 's capability to absorb and store heavy metals , sediments and minerals that would otherwise result @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ have a high tolerance for a wide range of salinities and contamination levels and perform an effective service in biofiltration and waste processing . They also play a vital role in nutrient uptake , fixation , trapping and turnover , and cycling of nutrients , even in the face of degrading conditions . <p> Biodiversity support : Mangroves form a nutrient-rich breeding ground for numerous species that thrive above and below the waterline . They harbour diverse flora and fauna , including rare and endangered species . Mangroves provide habitats for a wide range of plants and animals , contributing to overall ecosystem health and resilience . Mangrove forests are also a potential source of undiscovered biological materials that could benefit humankind , such as antibacterial compounds and pest-resistant genes . <p> Livelihood support : Local communities rely on mangroves for fishing , timber , non-timber forest products , and ecotourism , contributing to their economic well-being . Mangroves also offer medicinal herbs , as well as recreational and spiritual benefits to some local residents . <p> Despite their importance , mangroves are threatened by deforestation and degradation . They @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ development . Pollution from oil spills , sewage , and agricultural runoff can harm mangroves and the wildlife that depend on them . Finally , climate change is harmful to mangroves . Rising sea levels , more frequent and severe storms , and changes in temperature and rainfall patterns can destroy mangrove forests . <p> To safeguard these vital ecosystems , there is a need for a multifaceted approach that involves both local and global efforts . This can be achieved by raising awareness , implementing sustainable management practices , restoring degraded areas , enacting policies and regulations , as well as fostering international cooperation . <p> Advertisement <p> This story is published in partnership with Report for the World , a global service program that supports local public interest journalism .

@@100403782 <h> Vertiv Issues Updated Guidance For Data Centres During Extreme Heat <p> Summer in the northern hemisphere has just started , but already devastating heatwaves have washed over much of the U.S. , Mexico , Canada , Europe , Asia and parts of Africa . <p> Summer in the northern hemisphere has just started , but already devastating heatwaves have washed over much of the U.S. , Mexico , Canada , Europe , Asia and parts of Africa . <p> Widespread wildfires in Canada have triggered air quality alerts across that country and much of the eastern half of the U.S. Similar extreme heat events across Asia have caused widespread power outages , and temperatures in countries across Europe and Northern Africa , such as Algeria and Tunisia , continue to break heat records . <p> Climate change has made the past eight years the hottest on record , but with an El Ni ? o weather pattern compounding the issue this year , many forecasts anticipate record-breaking temperatures in 2023 . The sizzling outdoor temperatures and their aftermath create significant challenges for data centre operators who already wage a daily battle with the heat produced within their facilities @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ risks associated with extreme heat . These include : <p> Clean or change air filters : The eerie orange haze that engulfed New York City was a powerful visual representation of one of the most immediate and severe impacts of climate change . For data centre operators , it should serve as a reminder to clean or change air filters in their data centre thermal management systems and HVAC systems . Those filters help to protect sensitive electronics from particulates in the air , including smoke from faraway wildfires . <p> Accelerate planned maintenance and service : Extreme heat and poor air quality tax more than data centre infrastructure systems . Electricity providers often struggle to meet the surge in demand that comes with higher temperatures , and outages are common . Such events are not the time to learn about problems with an uninterruptible power supply ( UPS ) system or cooling unit . Cleaning condenser coils and maintaining refrigerant charge levels are examples of proactive maintenance that can help to prevent unexpected failures . <p> Activate available efficiency tools : Many modern UPS systems are equipped with high-efficiency @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ draws from the grid . Heatwaves like those we 've seen recently push the grid to its limits , meaning any reductions in demand can be the difference between uninterrupted service and a devastating outage . <p> Leverage alternative energy sources : Not all data centres have access to viable alternative energy , but those that do should leverage off-grid power sources . These could include on- or off-site solar arrays or other alternate sources , such as off-site wind farms and lithium-ion batteries , to enable peak shifting or shaving . Use of generators is discouraged during heat waves unless an outage occurs . Diesel generators produce more greenhouse gas and emissions associated with climate change than backup options that use alternative energy . In fact , organisations should postpone planned generator testing when temperatures are spiking . <p> " These heatwaves are becoming more common and more extreme , placing intense pressure on utility providers and data centre operators globally , " said John Niemann , senior vice president for the global thermal management business for Vertiv . " Organisations must match that intensity with their response , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ own power and cooling systems , but on the grid as well . Prioritising preventive maintenance service and collaborating with electricity providers to manage demand can help reduce the likelihood of any sort of heat-related equipment failure . @@100470799 <p> The IMNHC 2023 endorsed the right to quality care for women worldwide , amidst rising conflicts and humanitarian crises , particularly in Asian and African nations like Nigeria , where the strain on maternity and newborn health services is already high . <p> As of today , around 60 million people in the Horn of Africa are urgently in need of support , 15.3 million people require humanitarian assistance in Syria . <p> Meanwhile , about 2.5 million people have been displaced since the onset of the conflict in Sudan . Due to the impacts of climate change , conflict , and poverty , many countries are witnessing increasing humanitarian and fragile contexts worldwide , Salad said . <p> According to the 2023 Global Humanitarian Overview report , a staggering 339 million people will need humanitarian assistance and protection in 2023 . Among them are millions of pregnant people , of which 15 percent are at risk of developing life-threatening complications that require skilled care at birth . <p> Humanitarian crises drastically affect some already fragile health systems , including maternal and newborn health outcomes . The 2023 IMNHC bemoaned that 64 percent of global maternal deaths , @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ stillbirths happen in the 29 countries with UN Humanitarian Appeals in 2023 . The Mortality in Humanitarian Settings Dashboard confirmed the figures . It noted that these deaths are often directly linked to causes such as hemorrhage , infections , blood pressure disorders of pregnancy , complications from delivery , and unsafe abortion . <p> Other factors contributing to maternal and newborn deaths , as often witnessed in crisis-affected settings , include a dysfunctional or deteriorated health infrastructure with stock-outs in essential drugs , lack of adequate supplies , utilities , and equipment , and shortages of health workers ( examples are midwives ) . <p> POLL <p> Decades of global humanitarian crises , including the COVID-19 pandemic , highlight an unfortunate and recurring pattern : the decreased prioritization of maternal and newborn health , including the lack of prioritizing midwifery as a key strategy for reducing maternal and newborn deaths . <p> Aside from countries ' humanitarian focus on putting already limited resources into preventing infectious diseases and addressing other basic needs of the population , there 's another reason for the lack of prioritization : gender inequality . @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ essential services for women . It is also gender inequality that excludes most women from holding leadership roles in health . <p> To mark the 2023 World Population Day , which is celebrated under the theme of " Unleashing the power of gender equality : Uplifting the voices of women and girls to unlock our world 's infinite possibilities , " Salad called for gender equality . <p> Salad underscored the importance of advancing gender equality to improve maternal and newborn health in the context of growing population-related concerns , such as climate change , pandemics , and conflicts . <p> The UNFPA Jordan Sexual and Reproductive Health Specialist listed important prerequisites to create a more secure space for improved maternal and newborn care . <p> " If we want to create a more stable , peaceful , and resilient world of infinite possibilities . Kanem said , " The relationship between reproductive autonomy and healthier lives is an uncontested truth : as women are empowered to make choices about their bodies and lives , they and their families thrive -- and their societies thrive as well . " This is also critical for women in crisis settings who often face human rights violations and denial of access to life-saving health services when needed . Humanitarian crises highlight the fragility of progress made on gender equality -- with often dramatic increases in gender-based violence cases and obstacles in reaching groups left behind . And farmers should have all the tools they need to adapt to the effects of climate change and produce the food Africans need . <p> That 's why our foundation supports partners across Africa working to make birth safer , get life-saving vaccines to children , increase agricultural productivity and make food more nutritious . Young people depend on these basics to reach their full potential , and countries need them to grow and thrive . <p> Advertisement <h> Prioritise the most effective interventions <p> Throughout my visit , I met with impressive Nigerians working on innovations that can yield dramatic results at a relatively low cost . It 's also about making sure it 's spent well . <p> For example , one stubborn problem in Nigeria is the high rate of anaemia among pregnant women , which can cause @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Research shows that giving expectant mothers an intravenous infusion of iron , which takes only minutes and lasts an entire pregnancy , could save thousands of lives and protect the futures of millions of children . In Lagos , I met with Professor Bosede Afolabi , a partner of our foundation , as she administered this effective treatment and we discussed efforts to train more health workers throughout Nigeria on the practice . <p> Improving childbirth conditions is one of 12 high-impact , low-cost interventions that the Danish researcher Bjorn Lomborg highlights in an inspiring new book , ' Best Things First ' . Lomborg also notes the transformative potential of agricultural productivity . Spending an additional $5.5 billion per year on agricultural R&amp;D , he found , would yield annual benefits of $184 billion by reducing malnutrition , helping farmers adapt to climate change , and lowering food costs . That 's an amazing $33 return on every dollar . <p> In Lagos , I met with several scientists delivering on this promise , with solutions that include a high-yield cassava variety , digital tools to help farmers in @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ to protect against deadly aflatoxins , and a fertilizer that can increase the productivity of soybean crops by as much as 45% at a fraction of the cost of traditional fertilizer . <p> Advertisement <h> Get life-saving products to everyone who needs them <p> As with Professor Afolabi and her work with IV iron , these crop scientists were n't just creating innovative products ; they were thinking creatively about how to distribute their products and inform farmers about them across Africa . This focus on reaching everyone is critical for reducing dramatic gaps in health outcomes between rural and urban areas , rich and poor , men and women . <p> These and many other incredible innovations in the pipeline have the potential to save a lot of lives and improve even more -- but only if developers and designers are intentional about doing so . <p> There are so many worthy candidates for a country 's resources but high-impact interventions that reach everyone should be at the top of the list of priorities . I have every confidence that Africa 's young people wo n't just be the @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ . <p> Throughout this visit , I was continually struck by the enthusiasm of Nigeria 's young people to make a difference , and the creative ways they are harnessing innovative science and technology to accelerate progress and improve lives across Africa . The problems are persistent , but so are the people solving them . <p> Advertisement <p> Bill Gates is co-chair of the Bill &amp; Melinda Gates Foundation <p> Advertisement <p> Views expressed by contributors are strictly personal and not of TheCable.

His unrelenting indifference to the condition of the humanity of his compatriots often came out in the things he decided to make important or ignore . One of them is his kinship attachment to Niger Republic . In the dying days of his presidency , he seized every opportunity to underline his difficulty in presiding over fellow Nigerians towards who he had an unmistakably condescending attitude . He either saw us as a bit more difficult to handle than the cattle in his Daura ranch . <p> At other times , he bragged that his retirement would be more peaceful in Niger Republic than in riotous Nigeria . His preference for Niger Republic was not just a passing fancy or the butt of casual jokes . It was grounded in real attachment backed by dollars . He spent billions of dollars of Nigerian money to fund development projects like rail lines , oil pipelines , refineries etc. in Niger Republic . In what has graduated into a full -scale military coup , the Nigerien military has arrested and put away the president , sacked the government , suspended the constitution and nullified all functions of the democratic state . The two-year old democratic government that enabled the government has therefore been replaced by a military dictatorship . The television footages that have featured the rebellious soldiers does not indicate a group that is likely to hurry off from power no matter what the rest of the world says . In fact , after announcing the new leader as a certain General Abdourahmane Tchiani , former Brigade of Presidential Guards commander who had obviously been eyeing his former boss 's lavish privileges . Similar coups have occurred recently and in rapid succession in Mali , Guinea , Chad , Burkina Faso and , to some extent , Sudan where the clashing ambitions of rival generals and warlords has burst into an open civil war . Nearly all these regressions into autocratic rule are united by certain common factors . <p> Advertisement <p> The threat of jihadist terrorism and insurgency in the northernmost parts have created greater insecurity in all these countries . The national armies have been overwhelmed by jihadist insurgents and fighters . Climate change in the Sahel at large has created more desperate hunger , poverty and general economic distress in these agriculturally dependent countries . Economic pressure has translated into widespread unrest and urban protests . Protests have graduated into political unrest and dissatisfaction , making partisan democracy and its slovenly rituals untenable and unpopular . The existence of military establishments of ambitious and politicized officers has accelerated the recourse to coups . <p> The French who used to be @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ Africa have in recent times become unpopular and gone into a retreat mode given the political and economic burden of colonial era influence peddling . " <p> " Today , the World Meteorological Organisation and the European Commission 's Copernicus Climate Change Service are releasing official data that confirms that July 2023 is set to be the hottest month ever recorded in human history , " he said . <p> According to the official , " the World does not have to wait @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ and that short of a mini-Ice Age over the next few days , July 2023 will shatter records across the board " . <p> According to the data released , Mr Guterres stressed that July has already seen the hottest three-week period ever recorded ; the three hottest days on record ; and the highest-ever ocean temperatures for this time of year . <p> He said the consequences are clear and that they are tragic : children swept away by monsoon rains ; families running from the flames ; workers collapsing in scorching heat . <p> " For vast parts of North America , Asia , Africa and Europe -- it is a cruel summer . For the entire planet , it is a disaster , " he noted , adding that for scientists , " it is unequivocal -- humans are to blame " . <h> Way forward : " reducing emissions " <p> Mr Guterres said " they need ambitious new national emissions reduction targets from G20 members , and that there is a need for all countries to take action in line with my Climate Solidarity Pact @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ so that developed countries commit to reach net zero emissions as close as possible to 2040 , and emerging economies as close as possible to 2050 , with support from developed countries to do so , " he said . <p> He emphasised that all actors must come together to accelerate a just and equitable transition from fossil fuels to renewables -- " as we stop oil and gas expansion , and funding and licensing for new coal , oil and gas " . <p> He noted that credible plans must also be presented to exit coal by 2030 for Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development ( OECD ) countries and 2040 for the rest of the world . <p> " Ambitious renewable energy goals must be in line with the 1.5 degree limit , " he said . <p> The UN official said developed countries must reach net zero electricity by 2035 and 2040 elsewhere , as they work to bring affordable electricity to everyone on earth . <p> " Financial institutions must end their fossil fuel lending , underwriting and investments and shift to renewables instead . He said , " The world is @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ we are looking for is the energy solution that comes with environmental sustainability . " <p> The Chairman of the Renewable Energy and Energy Efficiency Association , Dr Talba Imamudeen , stressed the need to have a plan that sets out the timeline and targets of the Energy Transition Plan . According to him , this would help the plan to be under strict monitoring , thus making it achievable <p> According to the World Economic Forum , public offices like the Renewable Energy Association of Nigeria and the Rural Electrification Agency have provided training to build capacity and also provide technical assistance . As the country aims to transform its energy sector , there is a need to build technical capacity for solar developers and entrepreneurs . <p> Another initiative is that the government has embarked on the off-grid Electrification Strategy . The strategy aims to provide uninterrupted electricity supply for government hospitals , 10,000 mini-grids and 5 million solar systems for SMEs by 2023 . <p> Climate Action Africa , a social enterprise in Africa 's climate action ecosystem , suggests that the released funds from subsidy removal @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ projects such as solar , wind , and hydroelectric power . According to Climate Action Africa , investing in clean energy infrastructure not only reduces greenhouse gas emissions but also fosters long-term development and enhances energy security . <p> As fuel prices increase , Climate Action Africa urged individuals and businesses to adopt energy-efficient practices , resulting in lower energy use and waste . The social enterprise further stated that promoting the use of energy-efficient appliances , sustainable building designs , and environmentally friendly transportation systems will help Nigeria significantly reduce its carbon footprint . For instance , reducing the amount of waste disposed of by individuals and using alternative transport systems to reduce emissions . <p> More Nigerians are moving towards the use of solar sources of electricity due to the removal of fuel subsidy policy made by the government . According to Mr Tunde Adeagbo , a Solar Technical Officer , the number of people that have turned to using solar as a source of power has increased tremendously since the fuel subsidy removal . <p> He highlighted some advantages of using solar as a source of electricity @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , there is reduced electricity bills , low maintenance cost and low pollution , which limits its effect on the environment and the people . <p> Private-sector Intervention <p> Unlocking the necessary funds for this transformative endeavour requires a formidable partnership between the government and the private sector . Lance Abudu , Component Lead of Standalone Solar Home Systems said , " Despite an overall increase in global investment in technologies related to the energy transition , Sub-Saharan Africa received less than 1.5% between 2000 and 2020 . Unlocking the necessary capital will require intensive collaboration between government and the private sector , greatly increasing the likelihood of Nigeria achieving a just transition . " <p> In a private sector-concentrated meeting that was organised by the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet in collaboration with SEforALL , stakeholders in the private sector discussed the opportunities and challenges in Nigeria 's Energy Transition Plan . In response to the discussion , a private-sector working team was formed to support energy in Nigeria . <p> Some stakeholders such as the Dangote Group are taking steps to be part of the move @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ training exercise organised by the company , an Executive in the company , Haruna Adinoyi , stressed the need to sustain our environment . Haruna pointed out some of the practical actions that Dangote had already taken which includes the production of limestone cement and alternative fuel -- cutting down carbon emissions in the environment <p> Dangote Cement in its sustainability report for 2022 said the company prioritises enforcement of environmental sustainability . As such , it used waste as fuel for the pyro process , reducing the company 's consumption of fossil fuels . <p> Taking complementary actions to realise the goals of Nigeria 's ETP could be effective . These complementary plans include the modernisation of biomass utilisation , enhancing energy efficiency in SMEs and focusing on the removal of natural carbon . <h> Conclusion <p> Apart from reaping ecological benefits , Nigeria can also stimulate economic growth by creating jobs for its populace . Notably , the elimination of fuel subsidies gives a once-in-a-lifetime chance to transfer funding to sustainable energy initiatives . <p> The clock is ticking for Nigeria 's energy industry , and the time @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ @ , more sustainable environment would be long and difficult , but the potential rewards would be worth it . All parties must collaborate to diversify energy sources , reduce reliance on fossil fuels , and , ultimately , make power available to all .
